findings.title: Tag pin enforced only on the update path; a fresh clone adopts a moved tag silently
findings.description: _update_tag enforces the pin via a no-force fetch and a recorded-SHA comparison, both properties of an existing checkout. sync() routes to _clone() whenever .git is absent, and that path took no expected_sha and performed no comparison. The _update_tag docstring claimed to cover the fresh-clone case; it does not.
findings.exploit_scenario: Source pinned to tag v0.1.0 syncs and records SHA A. The local checkout is lost (this class's own _quarantine_non_repo_dir rename, a restored /data backup, or a recreated volume). Upstream force-moves v0.1.0 onto a commit adding an executable. Next sync takes the clone path and adopts the moved tag, returning success with a changed commit — so ent#236's fleet re-inject pushes the payload to every running agent, unattended.
findings.verification: Executed end-to-end against a local upstream repo. Before fix: success=True, moved_tag=None, action=cloned, commit changed from pinned SHA, backdoor.sh present on disk. After fix: success=False, moved_tag=True, checkout removed, backdoor absent.
findings.impact: Arbitrary third-party code injected fleet-wide into agent containers, defeating the feature's stated AC#5 supply-chain control, with a successful-looking sync.
findings.recommendation: Verify the resolved HEAD against the recorded SHA after a fresh clone and delete the checkout on refusal, since list_skills and injection read the working tree.
findings.fix_applied: _refuse_moved_pin_after_clone in skill_source_clone.py; regression test test_moved_tag_is_refused_on_a_FRESH_clone_too (fails without the fix) plus test_first_ever_clone_of_a_tag_has_no_pin_to_check.
